description: Issue #742 (Heritage half of the alias/Sprites shadowing fix, landed with #746), COMPLETED by ruling #833 / issue #838: with `heritage` ACTIVE, redefining a Heritage short alias raises `ol-reserved-word` exactly as redefining its canonical Core spelling does. Heritage is "alternate spellings only -- no new semantics" (`spec/conformance.md:150`), so `define pr` MUST be exactly as (il)legal as `define print`; before #742, `define print` raised and `define pr` was silently accepted **and the shadow took effect**, so a Heritage program could lose its `print` (`pr 7` then reported `ol-bad-token`). This fixture declares ALL THIRTEEN aliases in registry order and is therefore the whole symmetry table in one file. When #742 landed, only FOUR of the thirteen were reported: `pr`/`bf`/`bl`/`se` alias the **Core** primitives, while the nine turtle aliases resolved to a Turtle & Rendering table the checker deliberately did not consult (issue #783, awaiting a maintainer ruling). #833 supplied that ruling -- spec/grammar.md:382, "`define count`, `define forward`, and `define fd` are equally errors" -- and #838 wired `turtlePrimitiveArity` in, so all thirteen report and the file finally means what its name says. That the nine flipped with NO edit to the Heritage branch is the design working: the checker resolves an alias through `canonicalOfHeritageAlias` and re-runs the canonical's own lookup rather than keeping a second table, so the two spellings agree by construction. `params.name` is the **surface** spelling the learner wrote, at that name's own span (`pr`, never `print`) -- the contract #737 recorded for this code -- and `params.namespace` is gone, per spec/error-model.md:125. Paired with `heritage-alias-redefinition-legal-in-core`, which checks this exact source under Core alone and reports the same diagnostics -- an alias is a built-in name whether or not `heritage` is claimed (`spec/grammar.md:408`). That twin's file name no longer describes it; renaming is issue #842's. `"check": true` (semantic-checker only, no execution) because this is a checker rule: the procedures are never called and no events are produced.
